design_rationale:
WORKLOG / TEST DOSSIER — task 1 of home_claim_settlement (HomeGuard freeze burst, frozen 2026-09-22). Revision 2 (after policy-task audit round 1).

[Step 0 — draw and scope] draw_counts.py --task 1 printed {"prerequisite_problems": 2, "problems": 3, "factor_counts": [6, 4, 4]}. Occupied by task 0: home_ext_roof_denial_reversal, home_ext_structure_supplemental and their tools (wind/hail roof and other structures). Claimed here: home_ext_water_denial_reversal (6 factors, agent tool settle_denied_water_damage_028e176f), home_ext_mold_denial_reversal (4 factors, agent tool settle_denied_mold_remediation_0cacd0ff), home_ext_contents_supplemental (root, 4 factors, user tool accept_contents_supplemental_dc7651d7). Revision 2 moved the 6-factor draw from the contents computation to the water computation (the multiset [6, 4, 4] is unchanged): the contents computation now carries only allowances a contents adjuster actually pays. With task 1 all five extended policies are covered, pairwise disjoint.

[Why this is a good test] The customer asks only that the contents of her freeze claim HGC-26-109358 be settled the way the policy says. The contents rule carries two prerequisite sentences in the negated direction: "The personal property supplemental is not fixed until the dwelling water damage of the same claim carries a payment entry wherever the claim's first notice records a freeze or a sudden discharge of water." and "The personal property supplemental is not fixed until the mold remediation of the same claim carries a payment entry wherever that first notice records a freeze or a sudden discharge of water." The ledger shows peril freeze on the first notice while the dwelling damage (RC 11,800.00, dep 5,600.00) and the mold (RC 6,200.00) stand only as repeated-seepage denials. The agent must find that the water and mold reversals are the writes that put those payment entries on the claim, settle each with its own ladders, and then settle the contents on the world they leave. 16 home claim entries on three claims plus the LandlordGuard holding and ledger are reconciled.

[Problem-tree card] root home_ext_contents_supplemental. Edge 1 -> home_ext_water_denial_reversal, value_input, gate dw_abs, form state; condition: the claim carries a dwelling general payment entry instead of only the repeated-seepage denial; resolved_by settle_denied_water_damage_028e176f (agent). Evidence false at opening: home_claims.<k26_den_dw>.denial_reason = repeated_seepage, no dwelling home_claim_payment on HGC-26-109358, first notice peril = freeze. Edge 2 -> home_ext_mold_denial_reversal, value_input, gate mold_entries, form state; resolved_by settle_denied_mold_remediation_0cacd0ff (agent); evidence: <k26_den_mold>.denial_reason = repeated_seepage, no mold payment. Four-point test: ordering connective "not ... until" (negated direction; task 0's sentence is affirmative); a record-visible state (a payment entry of a named coverage part on the same claim); no tool, id or snake_case token; strength and scope 'wherever the first notice records a freeze or a sudden discharge of water'. Exactly one write produces each state: the dwelling-water state is a dwelling payment replacing a repeated-seepage denial on a freeze/discharge claim — the roof reversal writes roof surfacing on a wind or hail claim only; the mold state is written only by the mold reversal. Order: water (step 7), mold (step 9), contents (step 11); the two prerequisites commute (swapped replay gives identical values). Deletion sensitivity (actual runs): skipping the water reversal -> contents 2,562.00; skipping the mold reversal -> contents 3,636.00. The customer's own write is the root.

[Factor card — home_ext_water_denial_reversal, expected 8,100.00, baseline_result 3,700.00]
- single_event_deductible_credit (parameter, multi-source, cross-difficulty dwelling): LandlordGuard LGC-26-107715, loss 2026-01-26, payment carrying 1,000.00 < occurrence deductible 2,500.00 -> credit 1,000.00; the dwelling absorbs 1,500.00. Baseline 0 -> 7,100.00. Real practice: one freeze event across a household's policies with the same carrier borne under one deductible.
- water_depreciation_convention (method: which depreciation is recognized — materials-only share vs a cap vs as recorded): HO-3, RC 11,800.00 > 2,500.00 -> 5,600.00 capped at 40 percent = 4,720.00. Baseline recorded -> 7,220.00.
- water_drying_allowance (parameter): reported 2026-01-29, 3 days after the loss -> 4 percent = 472.00. Baseline 0 -> 7,628.00. Tiers keyed on report days only (no peril conjunct), all reachable.
- water_access_tearout (parameter): freeze (a frozen supply line inside the building) with RC >= 10,000.00 -> 6 percent = 708.00. Baseline 0 -> 7,392.00. Fall-through (a sudden discharge, whose wet-area tear-out is already inside the replacement-cost value) is reachable inside the policy's scope.
- water_plumbing_code_upgrade (parameter, multi-source): built 1972 (before 1980) AND ordinance-or-law 25 -> 5 percent = 590.00. Baseline 0 -> 7,510.00.
- water_hazmat_survey (parameter): built before 1978 -> 750.00. Baseline 0 -> 7,350.00.
[Factor card — home_ext_mold_denial_reversal, expected 8,728.00, baseline_result 6,200.00]
- mold_containment_scope (method: the formula changes — a second base, the claim's dwelling water damage, enters under full containment; a flat barrier charge under single-area containment; the estimate as is otherwise): HGC-24-134096 paid water loss 22 months back AND mold 6,200.00 >= 3,000.00 -> 6,200.00 + 10 percent x 11,800.00 = 7,380.00. Near-miss: HGC-23-121574 at 38 months is outside. Baseline -> 7,548.00.
- mold_clearance_testing (parameter): 6,200.00 >= 5,000.00 -> 650.00. Baseline -> 8,078.00.
- mold_antimicrobial_category (parameter): reported 3 days after the loss (3 to 7 days: grey water) -> 4 percent = 248.00. Baseline -> 8,480.00. Keyed on how long the water stood (clean -> grey -> black), not on the peril (revision 3, R2-O3).
- mold_duct_cleaning (parameter): dwelling water damage 11,800.00 >= 10,000.00 -> 450.00. Baseline -> 8,278.00. Fall-through (wet area below 4,000.00) reachable.
Cap 10,000.00 less mold issued for losses in the 12 months before the call (0.00) not reached. Payee insured (co-payee rule reaches only dwelling and other structures).
[Factor card — home_ext_contents_supplemental, expected 4,772.00, baseline_result 0.00]
- contents_settlement_method (method): RC 14,200.00 > 2,500.00 AND release 3,800.00 (documented 12,900.00) stands -> 12,900.00. Baseline ACV 9,100.00 -> 972.00.
- contents_cleaning (parameter, multi-source): mold payment entry (step 9) AND RC >= 5,000.00 -> 8 percent = 1,136.00. Baseline -> 3,636.00.
- contents_packout (parameter, multi-source): dwelling payment (step 7) RC 11,800.00 >= 10,000.00 -> pack-out and storage 5 percent = 710.00. Baseline -> 4,062.00.
- contents_saturated_handling (parameter): freeze -> 3 percent = 426.00. Baseline -> 4,346.00.
Contents deductible (plain, declared override): occurrence 2,500.00 less same-event share 1,000.00 (LandlordGuard same-date deductible) less 1,500.00 on the dwelling entries -> 0.00; before the water reversal it is 1,500.00.

[Base-invariant card] Subject home_claim_payment for all three writes: home_claim_settlement gate claim_opened satisfied by first notice <k26_rep> (claim_number bound to each write); home_roof_settlement, home_water_limitations, home_depreciation_recovery govern with no gate on a payment (policy_scope). No time gate. Overwrites declared: water — the water_limitations sudden/freeze-with-aop sentence (single-event credit) and the settlement sentence; mold — the per-term mold aggregate sentence (12-month window), the mold holdback sentence (no depreciation on a service), the settlement sentence; contents — the settlement sentence AND the base 'One deductible applies per occurrence ... until used up' sentence (same-event share).

[Business-object card] Target claim HGC-26-109358 (latest first notice, peril freeze, reported 2026-01-29). Included: <k26_den_dw>, <k26_den_mold>, <k26_pay_pp>, <k26_hold_pp>, <k26_rel_pp>, <k26_recov_pp>. HGC-24-134096 read only by the containment ladder, HGC-23-121574 only as the near-miss; LandlordGuard rows read-only evidence.

[Persona design] A night-shift pediatric nurse, brisk; volunteers only the contents complaint and on-file facts; only when asked: phone, DOB, ZIP, email, mortgagee, the LandlordGuard duplex and its same-night freeze. Passive consent to preliminary work; accepts the figure and payee read to her; closes when told it is issued. No mention of walls, mold or denials.

[Standard solution] find_customers -> verify (phone + DOB) -> find_home_policies -> find_home_claims -> find_dwelling_policies -> find_dwelling_claims -> settle_denied_water_damage_028e176f (acv_initial, withheld 4,720.00, deductible 1,500.00, 8,100.00, insured_and_mortgagee) -> settle_denied_mold_remediation_0cacd0ff (acv_initial, 8,728.00, insured) -> customer accept_contents_supplemental_dc7651d7 (4,772.00, insured).

[Draft recomputation from the visible context] The contents rule holds the supplemental until the dwelling water damage and the mold carry payment entries on a freeze claim; the ledger shows only denials; the two reversal rules replace them; recomputing gives 8,100.00, 8,728.00 and 4,772.00, identical to gold. Traps: HGC-23 at 38 months; the 2,500.00 absorbed by the February contents entry; the mold payee; the 1,300.00 contents holdback still standing.

[Revisions]
- v1 initial authoring.
- v2 (audit round 1): T1-R1/G-3 — the contents rule now follows the base absorption order (occurrence deductible less the dwelling and other-structures entries) with the same-event share stated and the base 'One deductible applies per occurrence ... until used up' sentence declared in overwrite; under the declared override the contents absorb 0.00 on this world (LandlordGuard share 1,000.00 + dwelling 1,500.00 bear the whole 2,500.00); pure base, which knows no same-event share, would leave 1,000.00, and it is the declared override that removes that reading. G-4 — the same-event share makes a LandlordGuard deductible >= the occurrence deductible leave nothing to the contents, and the contents rule now carries the waiver sentence. T1-R2/G-1 — mold containment rewritten as a genuine method (a second base enters; a flat barrier otherwise). G-2 — the drying ladder drops the peril conjunct; access and duct ladders re-keyed so every tier, the fall-through included, is reachable inside the scope; the peril-scoped duct fee became a wet-area fee. T1-R3/G-7 — companion-line factor removed; O-9 prompt replacement removed; O-6 disposal replaced by a saturated-goods handling allowance that only water losses incur; the 6-factor draw moved to water (plumbing code-upgrade and hazardous-material survey, the latter moved from mold where it fit less). O-8 — single-area tier is a barrier charge, not clearance testing. O-10 — water baseline now carries 'Before any single-event credit, the deductible left ... is the whole occurrence deductible' and lists wind_hail_deductible_minimum. O-11 — mold rule and tool say remediation carries no depreciation; the base mold holdback sentence is declared. O-12 — disposal RC>0 condition gone; pack-out tier 2 covers a dwelling payment with RC below 10,000.00 including 0.00. G-5 — waiver sums count payment entries that replace no denial. Seed: report date moved to 2026-01-29 so the drying and antimicrobial ladders sit on non-fall-through tiers. Re-run results: water 8,100.00, mold 8,728.00, contents 4,772.00; skip water 2,562.00, skip mold 3,636.00.

- v3 (audit round 2): task 1 passed. R2-O1 — the single-event credit and the contents same-event share now count only same-date LandlordGuard freeze or sudden-discharge claims (compute filters dwelling_claims.peril), matching the prose; LGC-26-107715 is a freeze claim, so values are unchanged. R2-O3 — the mold antimicrobial ladder is keyed on water age (reported within 2 days / 3 to 7 / more than 7), not on the peril; the water access fall-through now explains that a sudden discharge's wet-area tear-out is already inside its replacement-cost value. R2-O4 — the hazmat sentence now says the wet walls of every reversed water loss are cut out, so it no longer conflicts with the access wording. R2-T1-O1 — the v2 note's 'readings coincide' wording is corrected above. Values unchanged: water 8,100.00, mold 8,728.00, contents 4,772.00.
user_scenario: You are Philippa Rosenkranz-Adeyemi, a night-shift pediatric nurse who owns the house at 86 Brambleton Court in Pickerington, Ohio. You are brisk and practical, you call between shifts, and you would rather hear a clear answer than small talk. During the January 26, 2026 cold snap a pipe froze and burst upstairs; your claim number is HGC-26-109358. Your living-room furniture, rugs and a lot of household things were ruined; you were paid for them in February, you replaced them over the spring, sent in the receipts, and a second contents check came at the end of June. What you are calling about is the contents part of that claim: you were told the contents payments were final, but you want the contents part checked and settled completely the way your policy says. You do not know how the policy works it out and you do not suggest any figure of your own. You open by giving your name and saying you are calling about the contents on your freeze claim. When the agent asks you to confirm who you are, you give your phone number, 216-730-5582, and your date of birth, 1983-02-14; only if they ask for more do you add your ZIP code, 43147, or your email, p.rosenkranz.adeyemi@tallgrassmail.com. If the agent asks about the mortgage, Fairfield Heritage Credit Union holds it, loan number 1402-117-6385, exactly as on file. If the agent asks whether you have other Larkspur policies, you say you also insure your rental duplex at 73 Lockbourne Street in Canal Winchester with a LandlordGuard policy, that the pipes froze there the same night, and that LandlordGuard paid that claim; you do not remember the amount. If the agent tells you that other parts of the claim have to be put right before the contents can be settled, you tell them to go ahead with whatever the policy calls for and you ask nothing more about it. Whatever is still owed on the contents, you want to accept it yourself: once the agent tells you the figure and hands the acceptance over, you accept it on claim number HGC-26-109358 with exactly the amount and payee the agent reads you, without rounding or changing anything. If the agent says nothing more is owed on the contents, you accept that. Once you hear that the contents supplemental has been accepted and issued, you say thanks, you have to get some sleep before your shift, and you end the call.

Closed on payment with nothing withheld.

acv_initial: 6,400.00 - 1,100.00 - 2,500.00 = 2,800.00, >= 2,500.00 with mortgagee on file -> insured_and_mortgagee.

Closed once paid and no holdback remained.
Freeze burst 2026-01-26 reported 2026-01-29 (3 days later), policy in force (term 2025-09-15 to 2026-09-15); freeze has no fixed reporting period.

Denied repeated_seepage on 2026-02-18 although the first notice records freeze, a covered sudden loss; RC 11,800.00 and depreciation 5,600.00 recorded. This is the open item the water reversal settles.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.home_policy_id: c0d8773c-07aa-4f06-8e6c-9a17471040e5 — Id class; the docstring asks for the policy reference returned by the home policy lookup for the verified customer, and step 2 returns one HomeGuard policy, HG3-1609-2254. argument_uniqueness_tracing.claim_number: HGC-26-109358 — Verbatim class; the customer's line 'your claim number is HGC-26-109358' and the latest first-notice entry <k26_rep> on the policy ('The claim concerned is the latest first-notice entry on the policy'). Uniqueness: HGC-24-134096 and HGC-23-121574 are earlier first notices.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.source_entry_id: 859630b9-01d5-40ab-86ad-1b7f1d3f4c63 — Id class; the docstring asks for 'the repeated-seepage denial entry of the dwelling damage that this payment replaces'; the claim carries exactly one dwelling denial with denial_reason repeated_seepage. Uniqueness: the mold denial is a different coverage part and belongs to the mold reversal.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.payment_type: acv_initial — Enum class; rule 'The payment is replacement_cost_full when the covered amount is the full replacement-cost value and acv_initial otherwise, with the depreciation recognized withheld'; the replacement-cost value 11,800.00 is above the HO-3 Premier no-holdback threshold 2,500.00, so the covered amount is not the full value. Uniqueness: replacement_cost_full needs a value at or below 2,500.00.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.depreciation_withheld: 4720.00 — Fixed-format class, USD 2 decimals; 'on an HO-3 form with a replacement-cost value above that threshold, the depreciation recognized is the recorded depreciation but never more than 40 percent of the replacement-cost value': min(5,600.00, 40% x 11,800.00 = 4,720.00). Uniqueness: the recorded 5,600.00 exceeds the cap; the HO-5 materials-only convention does not apply to an HO-3 form.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.deductible_applied: 1500.00 — Fixed-format class, USD 2 decimals; occurrence deductible for a freeze = all-other-perils deductible 2,500.00; LandlordGuard LGC-26-107715 with the same date of loss carries a payment with 1,000.00 deductible, below 2,500.00, so the single-event credit is 1,000.00; waiver threshold 0 on HO-3 Premier; the dwelling absorbs min(2,500.00 - 1,000.00, covered 7,080.00) = 1,500.00. Uniqueness: the 2,500.00 on the February contents entry reflects the original misreading, not the declarations.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.amount: 8100.00 — calculated: covered 11,800.00 - 4,720.00 = 7,080.00 (water_depreciation_convention: HO-3 cap of 40 percent); less deductible absorbed 1,500.00 (single_event_deductible_credit: LandlordGuard same-date payment carrying 1,000.00 < 2,500.00 -> credit 1,000.00); less dwelling money already issued on the claim 0.00; plus drying 4 percent (reported 2026-01-29, 3 days after the loss), access tear-out 6 percent (freeze, RC >= 10,000.00) and plumbing code-upgrade 5 percent (built 1972, before 1980, ordinance-or-law 25) = 15 percent x 11,800.00 = 1,770.00; plus hazardous-material survey 750.00 (built before 1978); 7,080.00 - 1,500.00 + 1,770.00 + 750.00 = 8,100.00, floored at 0.00 and rounded to the cent.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.payee: insured_and_mortgagee — Enum class; base payee rule 'A dwelling or other_structures payment at or above mortgagee_copayee_threshold is payable to insured_and_mortgagee when a mortgagee is on file'; 8,100.00 >= 2,500.00 and Fairfield Heritage Credit Union is on file. Uniqueness: insured applies only below the threshold or without a mortgagee.

edges.condition: Where the claim's first notice records peril freeze or water_sudden_accidental, the claim carries a dwelling general home_claim_payment entry (with its deductible and replacement-cost value) rather than only a repeated-seepage denial of the dwelling damage.
edges.policy_source: The personal property supplemental is not fixed until the dwelling water damage of the same claim carries a payment entry wherever the claim's first notice records a freeze or a sudden discharge of water.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The first notice records freeze, yet the claim carries no dwelling payment entry: the dwelling water damage stands only as a repeated-seepage denial, and the whole 2,500.00 deductible sits on the contents entry.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The water reversal writes a dwelling payment carrying deductible 1,500.00 and RC 11,800.00: dw_abs 0.00 -> 1,500.00 (the contents deductible 2,500.00 - 1,000.00 same-event share = 1,500.00 -> 0.00) and the pack-out ladder moves from 0 to 5 percent.

edges.condition: Where the claim's first notice records peril freeze or water_sudden_accidental, the claim carries a mold home_claim_payment entry rather than only a repeated-seepage denial of the mold remediation.
edges.policy_source: The personal property supplemental is not fixed until the mold remediation of the same claim carries a payment entry wherever that first notice records a freeze or a sudden discharge of water.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The claim carries no mold payment entry: the mold remediation stands only as a repeated-seepage denial.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The mold reversal writes a mold payment entry: mold_entries 0 -> 1 and the cleaning ladder moves from 0 to 8 percent.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The two prerequisites are parallel and commute: replaying the mold reversal before the water reversal gives mold 8,728.00, water 8,100.00 and contents 4,772.00, the same values and the same terminal rows (the mold figure reads the dwelling water damage from the denial plus payments that replace no denial, so the reversal payment does not change it; the water figure reads no mold entry; each write's row id is a hash of its own arguments). Both must precede the contents supplemental.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the water reversal: the contents absorb 1,500.00 of deductible and the pack-out allowance drops to 0; the contents supplemental falls from 4,772.00 to 2,562.00, and the 8,100.00 dwelling payment is missing from the terminal ledger.
Skipping the mold reversal: the cleaning allowance drops from 8 percent to 0; the contents supplemental falls from 4,772.00 to 3,636.00, and the 8,728.00 mold payment is missing.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: The persona speaks only of the contents (furniture, rugs, household things) and the two contents checks; it never mentions walls, the dwelling damage, mold or any denial, and its only reference to preliminary work is the passive consent 'If the agent tells you that other parts of the claim have to be put right before the contents can be settled, you tell them to go ahead'.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: accept_contents_supplemental_dc7651d7 reads the claim's first notice only for its locating fields and writes the supplemental as given; it checks no dwelling or mold entry and never refuses. settle_denied_water_damage_028e176f and settle_denied_mold_remediation_0cacd0ff record their payments as given without judging eligibility or amounts.
